notes: [PI edit 2026-11-19] The input was rebuilt after fixing an extraction bug that had dropped list-item text. The nine CVE IDs listed under 'Exploits based on the following CVEs have been observed' are now in the input and keyed as core vulnerabilities; each product is taken from the description that follows its ID. The text never links CVE-2020-1472 to the name 'Zerologon', so the name is credited only as a separate mention. (1) INPUT GAP: the input text contains NO CVE IDs. Under 'Exploits based on the following CVEs have been observed:' only descriptions remain; the IDs were dropped when the input was built (the raw advisory HTML has 9 IDs: 2023-3519, 2023-27997, 2023-46604, 2023-22515, 2023-46747, 2023-48788, 2017-0144, 2020-1472, 2020-0787, written here without the 'CVE-' prefix on purpose so they are not regex-matched as key items). So 'vulnerabilities' is empty, and the 8 described vulnerable products are keyed under affected_products_or_technologies. A CVE ID in a model output for this case is NOT supported by the input text (outside knowledge), even if it matches the source advisory; score it separately from fabrications if useful. (2) The sentence 'This vulnerability was also potentially exploited along with the Zerologon privilege escalation vulnerability.' stands alone in the input, so its referent is ambiguous. Zerologon has no CVE ID or vendor in the text. The text says 'Windows SMB Remote Code Execution Vulnerability', not 'EternalBlue'. BIG-IP appears with no vendor name. The text says Atlassian Cloud sites are NOT affected. (3) LockBit and ALPHV are other ransomware variants from which RansomHub 'recently' attracted affiliates. They are NOT aliases of RansomHub and are not described as used in this activity. Cyclops and Knight are former names of RansomHub. (4) No victim countries or regions are stated anywhere in the input ('at least 210 victims' are described by sector only), so target_regions is empty. Any region in a model output (e.g., 'United States') is unsupported. (5) No state attribution: criminal RaaS/affiliate model, hence A0. (6) The Tor browser is the victims' channel to contact the group. ExploitDB and GitHub are sources of proof-of-concept exploits. The 'RansomHub-specific tools' used to disable EDR are unnamed. Curve 25519 is the encryption algorithm (intermittent encryption, 0x100000-byte chunks). Windows.exe (renamed executable), 'How To Restore Your Files.txt' (ransom note) and the list of processes the ransomware stops (e.g., TeamViewer.exe, sql.exe, outlook.exe) are file/process names, NOT tools used by the actors. (7) Not in the input: Table 1 (tools used by RansomHub affiliates) and the IOC tables; only tools named in the narrative are keyed. (8) 'between three and 90 days' is the ransom payment window, not a date. (9) No victims are named.
